claim: The staged indels use submitted REF/ALT strings that do not match VEP's normalized allele keys.
evidence: A runtime scan found five indels. Protein-coding transcript variant_allele is '-' for all four deletions and 'C' for the insertion, rather than the submitted ALT values 'C' and 'GC'. Three deletion frequency objects are likewise keyed by '-' instead of submitted ALT 'C'.
solver_impact: A universal exact-ALT filter on transcript consequences would discard every indel annotation; frequency extraction must separately respect the manifest's exact submitted-ALT rule rather than silently assuming transcript and frequency allele representations are identical.

claim: One multiallelic ClinVar record's clin_sig array combines labels belonging to different alleles.
evidence: For submitted ALT C, the colocated T/C/G record has clin_sig=['uncertain_significance','benign'], while clin_sig_allele is 'C:benign;G:uncertain_significance'. The other 10 records with clin_sig observed by the probe had labels mapped to the submitted ALT.
solver_impact: Taking the highest-priority value from the unpartitioned clin_sig array can assign another allele's significance; allele-specific association must be preserved when applying the submitted-ALT rule.

claim: Canonical-first transcript selection is not equivalent to the manifest's consequence-first, canonical-on-tie ordering.
evidence: A scan of all 50 responses found 15 variants where VEP's most severe consequence was absent from canonical protein-coding transcript consequences. Examples include chr1_955641_G_A (overall missense_variant; canonical protein-coding consequences intron_variant/upstream_gene_variant) and chr1_1310876_CGGCTCTGGGTCACAGGT_C (overall frameshift_variant; canonical consequences upstream, intronic, or downstream).
solver_impact: Transcript ranking must establish the highest-priority coding consequence before using canonical status as a tie-breaker; filtering to canonical transcripts first changes selected genes and consequences.
